_comment: Single source of truth for the Test Suite matrix. The setup job runs .github/scripts/build-matrix.js, which reads this file, counts the scenarios in each suite folder, and computes the shard count automatically (ceil(scenarios / target)). Both the matrix jobs and the report job's reconciliation (.github/scripts/reconcile-suites.js) then use the SAME generated list (expected-suites.json artifact), so the 'expected suites' list can never drift from what actually runs. Add/remove suites here — never edit shard counts by hand.
_sharding_note: Sharding is dynamic and scenario-level. build-matrix.js counts PICKLES (Scenario Outline examples expanded) per suite folder and splits it into ceil(scenarios / config.<group>.target_scenarios_per_shard) shards. Test jobs run `cucumber-js <folder> --shard i/N`, which distributes scenarios evenly across shards regardless of which .feature file they live in — so a single heavy Scenario Outline file is spread across shards (the old file-index splitter could not do this). IMPORTANT: `target` bounds each shard's scenario COUNT, not its wall-clock TIME — cucumber's --shard is a pure round-robin with no duration/retry awareness. So a shard filled to `target` with slow or flaky scenarios (--retry 2 => up to 3 attempts each) can still approach the step timeout. The real safety net is the step timeout + reconciliation (reconcile-suites.js): a timeout goes RED and recovers partial counts, never a silent under-count like run #439. Keep targets low enough that a full, worst-case (high-failure) shard still fits the step timeout with margin; when a suite's per-scenario time or failure rate rises, LOWER the target here rather than assuming count alone is safe. History: run #439 (Hotels/Flights General Non Booking) and a later run (Flights Amadeus Non/Booking, Flights General Non Booking 2/2) timed out because hand-tuned shard counts fell behind suite growth; dynamic sharding removes that specific treadmill.

config._target_note: Shard count = max(count-based, duration-based), capped at scenario count. count-based = ceil(scenarios / target_scenarios_per_shard) — the safety FLOOR for suites with no timing history. duration-based = ceil(measured CPU-min / cpu_minutes_per_shard) — gives slower suites MORE shards using .github/suite-durations.json (regenerate via collect-durations.js). LOWER either value = more, smaller, safer jobs. non-booking runs --parallel 2, booking --parallel 1 (heaviest scenarios). The per-shard wall-time warning in the test jobs (warns at ~70% of the step timeout) is the real-time backstop when a shard still trends hot.
